Name: Pyaasa
Review: “तुम्हारी है तुम ही सँभालो ये दुनिया ये दुनिया अगर मिल भी जाए तो क्या है” No surprise that Pyaasa is considered one of the greatest Hindi films ever made. Guru Dutt didn’t just make movies; he made poetry walk, cry, and burn. Sahir Ludhianvi didn’t just write lyrics; he spilled every heartbreak, every betrayal, every unspoken scream. The black-and-white frames? More colorful than half the movies today. Every shot is poetry in motion, every song a revolution in itself. Released in 1957, yet still untouchable. Some films fade. Pyaasa stays. Absolute cinema. Immortal.

Name: Dhoondte Reh Jaaoge
Review:
Dhoondte Reh Jaaoge sits right in that “so bad it’s good” tier alongside Tees Maar Khan. If you’re the type to unironically quote Tees Maar Khan or consider Entertainment a masterpiece, this is essentially your Citizen Kane.
It is loud, mindless, and completely devoid of logic, offering nothing but 100% pure, unfiltered entertainment. The movie-within-a-movie segments are absolute brainrot.

*Cinema died here, but at least it died laughing*

Name: Dhurandhar The Revenge
Review: Finally, an Indian director who gets it. I’ve spent years watching Hollywood spy flicks wishing we’d pull it off, and this is such a relief. No over-the-top nonsense-just pure, calculated detailing and a background score that actually breathes with the scenes. It’s a technical masterpiece for Indian cinema...

Name: The Odyssey
Review:
came expecting a bunch of guys fighting with swords, but ended up getting emotionally destroyed.

First, Agamemnon's outfit was insanely cool. My man walked into the Trojan War looking like he owned the place. Peak Greek fashion.

Then the story hits you way harder than expected. I thought it would just be monsters and adventures, but somehow I'm crying over a dog that waited 20 years just to see its owner one last time. That scene was brutal.

At the end of the day, *The Odyssey* is just the story of a guy who made one bad decision, upset a sea god, got lost for 10 years, came home to find 100 random dudes eating his food, and solved the problem with a bow and a lot of arrows.

Absolute cinema.
